subject: religious-studies
source_note: Topic structure follows the Cambridge IGCSE IGCSE Religious Studies specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.name: Paper 1: Worship, Beliefs, Scriptures & Sacred Places
units.blurb: The first three content sections, studied for two chosen religions

units.name: Paper 2: Festivals, Fasts, Family Life & Social Action
units.blurb: The final three content sections, studied for two chosen religions

topics.name: Worship
topics.blurb: Forms of worship and devotion in the chosen religions

topics.name: Beliefs & Scriptures
topics.blurb: Core beliefs and the sacred texts of each religion

topics.name: Sacred Places
topics.blurb: Places of pilgrimage and of religious importance

topics.name: Festivals & Fasts
topics.blurb: Major festivals, fasts and their meaning

topics.name: Rites of Passage; Religion & the Family
topics.blurb: Life-cycle rites and the role of religion in family life

topics.name: Religion & Social Action
topics.blurb: How belief leads to charity, service and social action

connections.why: Forms of worship express and are shaped by a religion's core beliefs
Sacred places gain their importance from key beliefs and scriptural events
Many places of pilgrimage are centres of communal worship
Festivals and fasts commemorate events and teachings from the scriptures
Festivals and fasts are major occasions of organised worship
Pilgrimage and festivals are often tied to the same sacred sites and seasons
Rites of passage enact beliefs about life, death and the family
Rites of passage are worship marking key moments in a believer's life
Teachings in the scriptures motivate charity and social action
Many festivals and fasts include giving to others and serving the community
Family and community values extend outward into wider social action
Worship and service are linked as expressions of devotion in practice
